b1.focus: Present tense: introductions, family, town, daily routine, work, shopping, appearance, belongings

b2.focus: Past tenses and the future: childhood, studies and work, the town, celebrations, housing, trips

b3.focus: Languages in everyday life, restaurants, mishaps, culture and sport, weather, big purchases, studies, health

intro.subtitle: Sounds, spelling, grammar, verbs and exceptions

x-temps-verbals.subtitle: All the tenses on one timeline: when to use which, the forms, and how they differ from English

x-nombres-calendari.subtitle: Numbers, telling the time, parts of the day, days of the week, months and seasons

b1-01.topic: Meeting people: name and spelling your surname, where you’re from, your mother tongue, where you live, your phone number; introducing someone else
grammar: ser, dir-se, viure: soc / em dic / visc — es diu, és de, viu a
the personal article: Soc la Maria, en Daniel
countries with an article: del Marroc, de l'Equador, del Perú
possessives with the article: el meu telèfon, la meva llengua, el teu, el seu
gender of nationalities: anglès / anglesa, marroquí / marroquina
b1-01.vocab: Countries, nationalities, languages; the alphabet; numbers 0–20 (digits 0–9 for phone numbers)
b1-01.extra: Spelling out loud: «be alta», «ela geminada», «ce trencada», «essa doble»; phone numbers digit by digit
b1-01.mission: Introduce yourself to a Catalan speaker (name, where you’re from, mother tongue, where you live) and ask them to spell their surname for you

b1-02.topic: Family: who's who by age and relationship, relatives' names, where they live and how old they are
grammar: demonstratives: aquest, aquesta, aquests, aquestes — Aquesta és la meva filla (“This is my daughter”)
plural possessives and “our, your”: els meus avis, la nostra filla
de + the personal article: el fill d'en Martí, la tia de la Marina
viure and tenir in every person: On viu la teva mare? Té 46 anys (age with “have”, not “be”)
també / tampoc: Jo també. Jo tampoc. (“Me too. Me neither.”)
b1-02.vocab: Ages and stages (nadó, nen, noi, home, dona gran) and relatives (pare, germà, avi, oncle, cosí, nebot, net, sogre, cunyat, marit, dona, parella)
b1-02.extra: Numbers up to 99: vint-i-u, trenta-dos, quaranta-sis; Catalan first names and two surnames
b1-02.mission: Show a classmate a family photo and tell them about three relatives: who they are, their name, where they live and how old they are

b1-03.topic: Where I live: street, number, floor and flat, what's near my home and how to say where it is using landmarks
grammar: viure and addresses: Visc al carrer de la Indústria, 49 (“I live at 49 Indústria Street”). A quin carrer vius? Quina és la teva adreça?
a / en: Visc a Viladepau, al carrer Nou, a la plaça Gran — but en una plaça (“in a square”)
ordinals for floor and flat: primer primera, segon segona — 3r 1a (tercer primera, “3rd floor, door 1”)
prepositions of place: al costat de, davant de / darrere de, a sobre de / a sota de, a prop de / lluny de, entre … i …
hi ha and és: Al carrer Nou hi ha una fleca (“There's a bakery”). On és el banc? — És davant de l'Ajuntament
b1-03.vocab: Streets (carrer, plaça, avinguda, rambla, passeig), shops and services (fleca, farmàcia, perruqueria, sabateria, llibreria, caixer, parada d'autobús, estació de metro, Ajuntament)
b1-03.extra: Numbers from 100 to 999 (cent, dos-cents, tres-cents vint-i-nou) and how to read addresses: C. de Còrsega, 377, 3r 2a, 08037 Barcelona; forms: nom, cognoms, adreça, població
b1-03.mission: Tell a classmate your address in Catalan (street, number, floor) and where your home is using landmarks: Casa meva és davant de…, al costat de…

b1-04.topic: Days and times: what happens on which day, mealtimes, telling the time, opening hours, birthdays, seasons and weather
grammar: days of the week: Quin dia és avui? El dilluns hi ha mercat / els dilluns (“on Mondays”); dilluns with no article — “this coming Monday”
-ar verbs in the 1st person: esmorzo, dino, berenem, sopo — A quina hora sopes?
telling the time: Són les tres i cinc, És un quart de quatre, Falten cinc minuts per a les quatre; del matí, de la tarda, del vespre, de la nit
opening hours: de 9 a 1, de dilluns a divendres; Comença a… i acaba a…; tancat
weather with fer: Quin temps fa? Fa calor, fa fred, fa vent, plou, neva, hi ha boira
b1-04.vocab: Àpats (esmorzar, dinar, berenar, sopar), parts of the day (matí, migdia, tarda, vespre, nit, matinada), days of the week, months, seasons, weather
b1-04.extra: The Catalan «quarts» system (dos quarts de nou = 8:30) — nothing like it in English; dates: El meu aniversari és el 23 de gener
b1-04.mission: Write a classmate a short “holiday message” in Catalan: where you are, what the weather is like, when you eat and what you do; give a time with quarts

b1-05.topic: Daily routine: what we do during the day, at what time, who with and how often
grammar: reflexive verbs: em llevo, et dutxes, es desperta, ens rentem les dents
present tense, 1st and 3rd person: treballo / treballa, plego / plega, llegeixo / llegeix
amb qui?: amb el meu germà, amb la seva dona, sol / sola
frequency: sempre, sovint, de vegades, de tant en tant, un cop per setmana, una vegada al mes, mai
anar a + place or infinitive: Vaig a la piscina. Va a comprar amb la seva dona
b1-05.vocab: Daily routine (llevar-se, dutxar-se, esmorzar, plegar, descansar, fer els deures, mirar la tele, anar a dormir), free time (passejar, fer esport, jugar a cartes, quedar amb els amics)
b1-05.extra: plegar — “to finish work, knock off”; vaig a comprar (“I’m going shopping”) vs vaig comprar (“I bought”); “I’m coming!” is «Ja vaig!»
b1-05.mission: Tell a classmate about your usual day and week in Catalan: when you get up, who you have lunch with, what you do once a week and what you never do

b1-06.topic: Work: what I do and where, what my job involves, my hours; if I'm out of work — what I'm looking for
grammar: treballar de, fer de, ser: Treballa de cambrer (“He works as a waiter”). Fa de dependenta. Soc professora (no article: not “a teacher”)
feminine job titles: cambrer / cambrera, metge / metgessa, administratiu / administrativa; lampista, paleta — one form
where I work: Treballo a Sabadell, a la papereria Mots, en un bar, en una fàbrica
what I do: despatxo, preparo, netejo, tallo; fer: faig classes, fas, fa
estar a l'atur, buscar feina de…: Busco feina de pintor (“I'm looking for work as a painter”)
b1-06.vocab: Jobs (cambrer, cuiner, dependent, infermer, metge, mecànic, perruquer, paleta, lampista), workplaces (oficina, fàbrica, taller, botiga, fleca, escola bressol), tasks at work
b1-06.extra: Feminine endings (-a, -essa, -iva) and job titles with one form; M'agrada la meva feina; fer festa — “to have the day off”
b1-06.mission: Tell a classmate in Catalan what you do and where (or what job you're looking for), your hours and what you do at work

b1-07.topic: Food and shopping: the shopping list, the market and shops, quantities and prices, informal tu and polite vostè at the counter, Catalan food through the seasons
grammar: voler in the present: Què vols? Vull cireres (“What do you want? I want cherries”). Què vol (vostè)? Vull pollastre. Què voleu? Volem llet
at the counter with vostè: Què vol? Alguna cosa més? (“Anything else?”) — Res més. Quant és? — Són 14 euros. Tingui (“Here you are”)
quant / quanta / quants / quantes + noun (“how much / how many”): Quant lluç vols? Quanta carn picada? Quantes mandarines?
quantities and packaging: un quilo de, mig quilo, 200 grams de, una dotzena d'ous, un pot de mel, una llauna de tonyina, un bric de llet, una ampolla de vi
where and from whom: a la carnisseria, a la peixateria, a la fleca, al forn, al mercat, al supermercat; el carnisser, la peixatera, la fornera, el dependent
b1-07.vocab: Food groups (fruita, verdura, llegums, làctics, carn, peix, cereals, dolços), seasonal fruit and vegetables, market stalls (parada) and shops, packaging (pot, llauna, bric, ampolla, garrafa, paquet, bossa), meals (esmorzar, dinar, berenar, sopar)
b1-07.extra: Catalan food through the seasons: escudella i carn d'olla in winter, tortell de Reis, bunyols and mona at Easter, coca de Sant Joan in summer, castanyes in autumn; berenar — afternoon snack
b1-07.mission: Do your shopping at a market entirely in Catalan

b1-08.topic: Appearance, clothes and personality: describing a person and comparing two people
grammar: ser, tenir, portar for looks: És alta i morena. Té els cabells llisos i els ulls verds (“She has straight hair and green eyes”). Porta ulleres i barba (“He wears glasses and has a beard”)
adjective agreement: ros / rossa, castany / castanya, pèl-roig / pèl-roja, gras / grassa; diminutives baixet, grassonet; one form: jove, gran, optimista, intel·ligent
degree: molt, bastant, força, una mica, més aviat; with a negative no… gaire (“not very”), no… gens (“not at all”): No és gens tímida; ho for an adjective: És alt? — No, no ho és (“No, he isn't”)
comparisons: més… que, tan… com: L'Ivan és més alt que les noies. La Rita és tan baixa com la Milena
clothes: porta un jersei de llana, una camisa de ratlles, de quadres (“a wool jumper, a striped / checked shirt”); colours: blau cel, blau marí; m'agrada el lila / m'agraden els colors clars
b1-08.vocab: Age (nen, noi, jove, de mitjana edat, gran), height and build, hair and hairstyles (llisos, arrissats, cua, monyo, trena, serrell), accessories (ulleres, arracades, mocador), clothes and shoes, colours, personality traits and their opposites (pacient / impacient, simpàtic / antipàtic, treballador / gandul)
b1-08.extra: Té els cabells llisos (the hair you have) but els porta llargs (how you wear it); estar for a state: Està una mica grassoneta, Estan contents; xerraire — chatty, tafaner — nosy
b1-08.mission: Describe a friend’s looks and personality so well that someone could recognise them

b1-09.topic: Belongings: what's in your bag and pockets, whose it is, what it's for and what it's like (size, shape, material, colour); what's in the classroom
grammar: De qui és? — És meu / meva, són meus / meves (“Whose is it? — It's mine”). És d'en Daniel, de la Miren; el meu, el teu, el seu: Aquest no és el meu
aquest / aquesta (“this”) and aquell / aquella (“that”), aquí and allà; això and allò: Què és això d'aquí? Què és allò d'allà?
servir per + infinitive (“to be for …ing”): Un paraigua serveix per no mullar-se; with a pronoun: per pentinar-te, per protegir-te els ulls
Hi ha algun / alguna…? — No hi ha cap… (“no … at all”); Hi ha algú? — No hi ha ningú (“nobody”); No porto res (“nothing”)
describing things: gros, petit, de mida mitjana; de fusta, de metall, de plata, de roba; rodó / rodona, quadrat / quadrada; plegable, de quadres
b1-09.vocab: What's in a bag and pockets (claus, cartera, moneder, mòbil, estoig, ulleres de sol, mocadors de paper, xiclets, pintallavis, paraigua, agenda), classroom objects (taula, cadira, pissarra, paperera, guix, ordinador), sizes, shapes, materials, colours
b1-09.extra: Plurals with a spelling change: butxaca → butxaques, -ga → -gues, -ja → -ges; the game «Veig, veig, què veus?» (“I spy”) — guess an object with yes / no questions
b1-09.mission: List in Catalan everything in your backpack

b1-10.topic: End-of-course party: the mayor's speech, radio interviews with the head of the school and a student, students introduce each other — review of Bàsic 1
grammar: questions with vostè: Vostè és d'aquí? Viu sola? Quin horari fa? Li agrada la seva feina? (“Do you like your job?”)

talking about yourself: Em dic Joaquim, però em diuen Quim (“but people call me Quim”). Soc de Barcelona, visc a Viladepau des de fa 15 anys. Fa set anys que soc alcalde (“I've been mayor for seven years”)
likes and dislikes: M'agrada molt la meva feina. El que no m'agrada gaire és… (“What I don't really like is…”)
introducing someone in the 3rd person: Es diu…, és del Marroc, la seva llengua materna és l'àrab, el seu pare…, viu amb…, fa de…
module review: looks and personality, daily routine, work and hours, address and phone number
b1-10.vocab: A party, a welcome speech, interviews; work and hours, holidays, the school year (inscripcions, cursos, exàmens), family, looks and personality
b1-10.extra: Ajuntament — town hall, in small towns also called casa de la vila; alcalde / alcaldessa — mayor; short forms of names: Joaquim → Quim
b1-10.mission: Ask a classmate 5–6 questions in Catalan and introduce them to the group: where they are from, what language they speak, where they live and work, what they are like

b2-01.topic: Childhood and youth: who I lived with, what I was like then and now, what I played; the people close to me
grammar: the imperfet: parlava, vivia, era (“used to / was …ing”)
de petit, quan era jove
comparing: abans… ara (“before… now”)
b2-01.extra: Imperfet of ser / estar / fer / veure
b2-01.mission: Write a paragraph about where and with whom you lived as a child

b2-02.topic: Studies and work: the education system, my education, working conditions, household chores, what you're doing right now
grammar: estar + gerund: Què estàs fent? (“What are you doing?”)
haver de + infinitive (“have to”)
past and present: abans treballava de…, ara treballo de…
b2-02.vocab: Education (ESO, batxillerat, FP, universitat), working conditions (horari, sou, contracte), household chores
b2-02.extra: The Catalan education system; false friends in work vocabulary
b2-02.mission: Read a job advert in Catalan and retell it

b2-03.topic: Daily routines of children, adults and older people; what people do at work; buying at the counter: the queue, the product, the price
grammar: reflexive verbs: where the pronoun goes
abans de / després de + infinitive
en at the counter: me'n posa mig quilo (“give me half a kilo of it”)
b2-03.extra: «Qui és l'últim?» — how to join the queue and order at the counter
b2-03.mission: Describe a typical day of someone in your family, and buy something at a counter, joining the queue in Catalan

b2-04.topic: The town then and now: services near home, transport, asking the way, getting a service sorted (a library card)
grammar: imperfet and present: abans hi havia…, ara hi ha… (“there used to be…, now there is…”)
directions: agafa el metro, gira a la dreta
vostè / vostès and polite requests: voldria, podria
the pronoun hi: hi vaig en bus (“I go there by bus”)
b2-04.vocab: Neighbourhood, transport, library, ajuntament, documents, forms
b2-04.extra: The Biblioteques de Barcelona network and the free library card
b2-04.mission: Get a library card using only Catalan

b2-05.topic: Celebrations and presents: choosing one, where to buy it, describing what you want in a shop; inviting and answering an invitation
grammar: the futur: regalaré
indirect object: li, els; doubling: li… a en Daniel
politely declining: Em sap greu, no podré venir (“I'm sorry, I won't be able to come”)
b2-05.vocab: Celebrations, presents, shops, in-store announcements, congratulations
b2-05.extra: The personal article en / na / l’ before names
b2-05.mission: Invite a friend to a celebration, and politely turn down someone else's invitation — in Catalan

grammar: comparisons: més… que, tan… com, millor, pitjor
hi ha / no hi ha cap
b2-06.vocab: Home, furniture, appliances, lloguer, pis, àtic
b2-06.mission: Describe your flat as if you were letting it

grammar: the passat perifràstic: vaig arribar (“I arrived”, not “I’m going to arrive”)
dates and years
fa + time: fa tres anys (“three years ago”)
b2-07.extra: How to say years: dos mil vint-i-sis
b2-07.mission: Tell a Catalan acquaintance how you moved to Barcelona

b2-08.topic: Trips: talking about a trip, comparing holiday places, nature parks, accommodation, ticket machines
grammar: the passat perifràstic: vam anar, vam dormir (“we went, we slept”)
transport and duration: en tren, trigar dues hores (“to take two hours”)
the pronoun hi: hi vam anar en cotxe
b2-08.vocab: Transport, accommodation (alberg, càmping, casa rural), nature, tickets
b2-08.extra: Catalan nature parks: Montseny, Aigüestortes, Cap de Creus
b2-08.mission: Plan a trip to a nature park in Catalan: transport, how many days, where to stay, what to see

b2-09.topic: How people change: appearance, personality and habits then and now; an important person in your life
grammar: imperfet and present compared
soler + infinitive (“usually”, “used to”)
ja no, encara
b2-09.vocab: Habits, looks, personality in the past
b2-09.extra: Passat perifràstic or imperfet: which one when
b2-09.mission: Compare yourself five years ago and now

b2-10.topic: Review of Bàsic 2, first health topics
grammar: the perfet: s’ha trencat
review of the past tenses

b3-01.topic: Languages in everyday life: who speaks which languages, how people learn them, how often I speak Catalan
grammar: guessing: deu ser de…, deu parlar… (“he must be from…, she must speak…”)
pronoms febles: putting it all together
tu and vostè
b3-01.vocab: Languages, language learning, neighbours and conversation
b3-01.extra: How to keep the conversation in Catalan when people switch to Spanish or English
b3-01.mission: For a week, speak only Catalan with your neighbours and shop assistants

b3-02.topic: Restaurants and cooking: choosing a restaurant, the menu, booking a table, apologising; recipes and Catalan dishes
grammar: the imperative: talla, afegeix, poseu
politeness: Voldria reservar una taula. Perdoni.
en and quantities
b3-02.extra: Catalan cuisine: pa amb tomàquet, escalivada, crema catalana
b3-02.mission: Write down your favourite recipe in Catalan

b3-03.topic: Mishaps: what has just happened, minor injuries and incidents, short phone calls, voicemail, the news
grammar: perfet and passat perifràstic
irregular past participles
b3-03.mission: Leave a voice message in Catalan: what has happened and why you can't come

grammar: suggesting: Per què no anem…? Què et sembla si…? (“Why don't we…? How about…?”)

grammar: the future: irregular forms
conditions: si + present, future

b3-06.topic: Buying a car: which vehicle suits whom, comparing models, credit, choosing a colour
grammar: giving an opinion: crec que, em sembla que
comparisons and superlatives: el més…
b3-06.vocab: Cars and other vehicles, features, colours, credit

pensar / tenir ganes de + infinitive
m’agradaria

pronouns with health verbs
